```c
static DWORD CALLBACK FormatDriveThread(PVOID pThreadParameter);   /* CALLBACK == __stdcall */
```

came back as a plain `unsafe fn`, i.e. **Rust's own convention**, and is then handed to
`SHCreateThread` to be called from a fresh thread. Nothing in the crate disagrees, because the
value only becomes a `LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE` at the FFI call. The tell is in the C: `CALLBACK`,
`WINAPI`, `NTAPI`, `APIENTRY` and `STDMETHODCALLTYPE` all decorate a *definition*, and every one
of them must survive as an `extern "..."` on the Rust `fn`. Grep the C tail for those five
before believing a bare `unsafe fn`.

**Where to spell it: `extern "system"`, not the literal the header used.** `system` IS stdcall
on i386-windows and IS the C convention on 64-bit, so one spelling is right everywhere; writing
the literal forces a `#[cfg]`-duplicated copy of the whole function per arch, and two bodies
that must be edited in lockstep drift. That is not hypothetical — shell32 carried four such
twins (`SIC_CompareEntries`, `sic_free`, `dde_cb`, `_DestroyCallback`) purely because the island
spelled the slot `stdcall`. The generator-side fix is `normalize_island_abi.py`, which projects
every ABI-identical fn-pointer slot to `extern "system"`; once an island has been regenerated
through it, the twins collapse to one body. A slot that comes from a `-sys` crate instead of the
island (`DLGPROC`, `LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE` — both ntdll-sys) has NOT been through it, so
re-declare that one API locally against an `extern "system"` fn-pointer, the way `prelude.rs`
does for `DLGPROC`. The ABI is unchanged; only the spelling is.

**A local re-declaration is not enough once a STRUCT FIELD carries the slot.** Re-declaring
`DialogBoxParamW` against a local `extern "system"` DLGPROC fixes the free function, but
`PROPSHEETPAGEW::pfnDlgProc` is typed `DLGPROC` *inside the island*, and a `pub type DLGPROC`
in the prelude does not retype a field of a struct the island emitted. A dialog-heavy module
hits both — netcfgx has twelve dialog procs plus two property-sheet page structs. The fix is
one profile line, `UNBLOCK="DLGPROC"` in `gen_driver_types.sh`: the island then emits its own
copy, `normalize_island_abi.py` spells it `extern "system"` on all three arches, and field and
free function agree, so ONE definition of each dialog proc serves every target. Without it the
crate needs a `#[cfg(target_arch)]` twin per proc — which is what netid-rust still carries, and
the twins had already drifted apart in incidental casts by the time anyone compared them.
Note the trap that makes this look optional: **Rust compares fn-pointer ABIs NOMINALLY**, so
`extern "system"` unifies with neither `extern "stdcall"` (i386) nor `extern "C"` (amd64/arm64)
even though it *is* each of them on that target. The mismatch is per-arch, so fixing i386 by
hand flips the error to the other two.

### Aggregates, arrays and unions across the FFI boundary
- **`i64` substituted for a by-value `_LARGE_INTEGER`** — i386 cdecl lowers an 8-byte
  aggregate differently from a scalar `i64`; amd64 hides it. Mirror the union type exactly and
  pass `*ptr`, not `(*ptr).QuadPart`.
- **A Rust `[T; N]` passed to a C-variadic is passed BY VALUE** — arrays do not decay. `%s`
  then consumes the first word as the pointer: i386 uefildr wedged in `strnlen(0x6f636553 /*
  "Seco" */, SIZE_MAX)`. Latent under TCG (unmapped reads return 0, scan ends instantly) and a
  multi-hour "hang" under WHPX/KVM, where every probe is a VM exit. amd64 accidentally works
  (Win64 passes >8-byte aggregates by reference). **`.as_ptr()` every array into a variadic.**
  Second instance, and it shows the shape a *macro* wrapper hides: msgina rendered
  `StringCchPrintfW(szBuffer2, _countof(szBuffer2), szBuffer, pgContext->UserName)` as a
  `macro_rules!` that spliced `$arg` straight into `wsprintfW`, so `UserName` — a
  `[WCHAR; 256]` — went by value and `%ws` read two characters of the user's name as an
  address. rustc says nothing: an array IS `Sized`, so it is a legal variadic argument. A macro
  wrapper is the worst place for this class because there is no declared parameter type
  ANYWHERE for a reviewer to compare against.
  Third and fourth instances (2026-10-04), after which it became a gate: the i386 DHCP client
  service died in msvcrt's printf engine on every boot that ran long enough to start Dhcp,
  reading 0x7374656e ("nets", from "netstack smoltcp adapter"), because dhcpcsvc logged
  `(*ip).name` by value at seven sites. msgina's three direct `wsprintfW(.., DomainName,
  UserName)` calls had it too. `scan_variadic_array_arg` (`vibeos-cli check`, empty baseline)
  resolves each `(*v).f` argument through v's declared type, since `name` is an array in
  `interface_info` and a pointer in the two dhcpcsvc structs beside it.
  Fifth (2026-10-10), the shape the gate could not see: a bare array VARIABLE through an
  ALIAS. sndrec32 passed `static mut str_mono: [u16; 10]` to `gprintf` (`pub use
  .._snwprintf as gprintf`) inside an `if c { str_mono } else { str_stereo }`, and died at
  0x00740073 ("st" of "stereo") painting its window on i386 only. The scanner now also flags
  a bare `static`/`let` array argument (a parameter or local of the name shadows it), follows
  `pub use .. as` aliases of a variadic, and checks both arms of an inline if/else.
- **`extern CCHAR Foo[N]` declared as `*const i8`** — Rust reads the first bytes of the buffer
  *as* the pointer (`"mult"` = 0x746C756D). Mirror the array type, or use a C accessor.
- **Cross-DLL DATA import indirection.** Under `raw-dylib` the `__imp_` load already yields the
  symbol's value, so an extra `*` reads the array's first bytes as a pointer → AV. Declare the
  same indirection ntoskrnl actually exports; the `*const *const` form in `fsrtlfuncs.h` exists
  only under `__CREATE_NTOS_DATA_IMPORT_ALIAS` and must not be copied. Conversely, a cohab
  driver referencing kernel **data** (`KeLoaderBlock`) needs `raw-dylib` on i386/arm64 (PE data
  imports need an `__imp_` thunk); amd64 tolerates a plain extern static and hides it. Declare
  it crate-locally — don't change shared `globals.rs`, the kernel needs the local form.
  pciidex.sys hit it with `InitSafeBootMode` and `HALDISPATCH` (undefined on all three arches).
  A kernel island now does this itself: `gen_driver_types.sh` runs
  `bindgen_data_imports.py`, which gives every `@ extern` (DATA) export of ntoskrnl.spec /
  hal.spec its own raw-dylib `+verbatim` extern block, so the translation reads the C's plain
  name. raw-dylib is right on **amd64 too** (pciidex.sys: one ntoskrnl.exe descriptor,
  `cmpl $0x1, (%r8)` through the slot); the hand-bound `__imp_` form there was never needed.
- **`[T; 0]` extern-array decl** `[§9.35]` — Rust bounds-checks the *declared* length, so the C unsized-
  extern idiom panics at index 0. Declare the real per-arch size.

### i386 no-SSE float ABI: an `f32`/`f64` value cannot cross a fn boundary
i686 usermode crates build `-sse,-sse2`, so rustc rejects any float **passed by value** — and
it checks at the *definition*, so `#[inline(always)]` does not help. Fine on no-SSE i386:
float math inside a body (x87), float pointers, float struct fields. Two fixes:
- **Internal C float helper → `macro_rules!`, not a fn** (`GDI_ROUND`, `_fmul`, `_lrintf`).
  Keep the macro's internal width matching the C — C does transforms in `double`; narrowing to
  f32 silently loses precision.
- **Exported fn taking FLOAT by value → cfg-split the signature.** i386 stdcall passes a
  4-byte FLOAT on the stack, bit-identical to a `u32`; amd64/arm64 pass it in a vector register
  and need the native `f32`. A plain `f32` won't compile on i386; a plain `u32` corrupts the
  others (`SetMiterLimit`).
- **User-mode crate route: re-enable SSE for that crate's build only.**
  `rust_staticlib_variant(... ENV "RUSTFLAGS=-C target-feature=+sse,+sse2")` on i386, the
  oleaut32/msvcrt pattern; sndrec32's `fseconds_total() -> f32` methods needed it. `port flip`
  now emits it for a crate whose code uses `f32`/`f64`. Never for kernel code.
- **A crate-PRIVATE helper is not exempt — give it `extern "C"`.** The `"Rust"` ABI passes
  f64 in xmm on x86, so a plain `fn helper(x: f64, xx: f64) -> f64` in a libm crate is rejected
  even though nothing outside the crate calls it; `extern "C"` uses x87/stack and compiles.
  This is why every float helper in `cnt-rust/src/cabi/math.rs` is `extern "C"`. Two traps
  around it: the rejection is **codegen-time, so `cargo check` cannot see it** — only a real
  `cargo build --target i686-pc-windows-gnu` with `-C target-feature=-sse,-sse2` will (a green
  amd64 + arm64 build proves nothing here); and the check fires per-ABI-classification, not
  per-mention, so a sibling `fn f(x: f64) -> (f64, f64)` returning through sret can sit right
  next to the rejected one and compile — don't conclude from it that plain `fn` is fine.
- **`f64::from_bits` / `to_bits` are themselves calls that pass an f64.** Moving a double
  through a soft-float boundary as its bit pattern (ftfd's private vsprintf, i386 KERNEL code)
  needs `core::mem::transmute::<u64, f64>`, which is not a call; `from_bits` hit the same
  rejection from inside `core`. A varargs double is pulled as `arg::<u64>()`: on all three
  targets `va_arg(double)` reads the same 8-byte slot.
- **So a THIRD-PARTY float crate (`libm`) cannot build there at all** — it is all Rust-ABI,
  and you cannot `extern "C"` someone else's crate. ucrtbase solved it by dropping to the
  SSE2 baseline (no kernel consumer; Microsoft's x86 ucrtbase is `/arch:SSE2`). That makes
  the x87-only `sdk/lib/crt` i386 `_control87`/`_statusfp`/`_clearfp` WRONG for that module:
  `fesetround` moved the x87 while every SSE2 add rounded in MXCSR. They now drive both units
  (Wine's versions, `ucrt-rust/src/fenv.rs`). Raising another module's baseline needs the same
  check.
- **`libm` ignores the FP environment by design** — Rust has no rounding modes. Its aarch64
  `rint` is `frintn` (always nearest, no inexact), so `rint(1.2)` under `FE_UPWARD` is 1. Any
  C function DEFINED by the current mode (`rint`, `nearbyint`, `lrint`, `llrint`) must not be
  a plain `libm` call: use `frintx`/`frinti` on arm64. On x86 libm's `x + 2^52 - 2^52` happens
  to round in MXCSR's mode.
- **`libm` is NOT musl for `pow`/`exp`/`log`** (or `exp2`/`log2`): those are FreeBSD msun's
  older e_pow.c and friends — under 1 ulp, but `pow(10, n)` misses the nearest double in 65 of
  601 cases (glibc 2, musl's current code 3). msvcrt's x87 `pow` got them right, so a straight
  swap regressed i386; the msvcrt winetest saw it because it builds its EXPECTED values with
  `pow(10, n)`. `sdk/lib/rust/musl-math` is a port of musl's ARM-routine versions, graded
  bit-exact against the musl C (`musl-math-difftest`). Check a crate's `origin:` header
  before calling it "the same code as X".
- **Generating coefficient tables from C: diff the generated values against the compiled C
  object, not against your reading of the source.** Two generator bugs shipped wrong tables
  that the Rust compiled and ran fine on: matching C designated initializers by POSITION
  (exp_data.c initialises `negln2hiN` before `shift`, unlike the struct), and stripping a
  float `f` suffix with `rstrip("f")`, which ate the last digit of every hex table integer
  ending in `f`. Both surfaced only as "exp-family mismatches, log-family exact" in the
  bit-exact fuzz; dumping `__exp_data` from the C object found them in a minute.

### i386 symbol lookup and asm aliasing
- **Three decoration schemes**: cdecl `_name`, stdcall `_name@N`, fastcall `@name@N`. A grep
  for the bare name finds nothing. Try all four forms or use `qemu/sym2addr.sh`.
- **`extern "fastcall"` is i386-only** — cfg-split every fastcall block and every
  `#[no_mangle] extern "fastcall"` export (`@Name@N` decoration is load-bearing for the cohab
  link). One private `_impl` + two thin cfg'd wrappers avoids duplicating bodies.
- **A `global_asm!` `.set _X, _X@0` alias must live in the crate that defines the target** —
  GAS evaluates it at assembly time, so across rlibs it emits an undefined reference instead of
  an alias.
- **LLVM COFF-i386 rejects `push offset <label>`** ("unsupported relocation type"); the
  `mov reg, offset` encoding works. Worse, bare `push <label>` is a silent **memory** push.
  Materialise into a provably-dead scratch register, then push it.
- **On i386 `ebx` is an ordinary `reg`: never `xchg` it around an instruction whose pointer
  operand is `in(reg)`.** Only x86_64 reserves rbx. The slist crate's i386 `cmpxchg8b` did
  `xchg {new_lo}, ebx` / `lock cmpxchg8b [{addr}]`, LLVM put `addr` in ebx, and the swap
  replaced the header pointer with the entry being pushed. Symptom: `InterlockedPushEntrySList`
  spins forever at 100% (or "succeeds" into the entry with the list unchanged); Wine's
  ucrtbase cpp test hung in `__std_type_info_name`. Shipped in ntdll.dll and ks.sys; ntoskrnl,
  built from the same source, allocated differently and was fine. Fix: pin the pointer to a
  fixed register (`in("edi") addr`, `[edi]` in the template). `scan_xchg_ebx_deref` gates it on
  every i386 build.
- **Verify an asm translation by disasm-diffing against the original `.obj`**, not by smoke —
  SEH/setjmp/CRT paths are barely exercised by a boot. `objdump -d` both (don't extract from a
  *thin* archive; objdump the on-disk `.obj`). Any diff beyond annotated reloc workarounds is
  real.

### Cohab link plumbing
- **A kernel DLL that imports only win32k cannot link `panic-common`'s `kernel` flavour.**
  GDI font and display drivers (bmfd, ftfd: `add_importlibs(ftfd win32k)`) have no ntoskrnl
  import library, so the panic path's `DbgPrint`, `KeBugCheckEx` and `RtlWalkFrameChain` are
  undefined (arm64 LINK_FAIL on ftfd.dll). Use the zero-extern `raw` flavour; scaffold now
  picks it from the target's `add_importlibs`.
- **`_tWinMain` / `_tmain` are tchar.h MACROS.** The CRT startup calls the real name
  (`wWinMain`/`wmain` in a UNICODE build), so a translated `#[no_mangle] fn _tWinMain` (sol,
  spider) is an `undefined symbol: wWinMain` at link. `port integrate` renames them.
- **A tree-consensus extern that no import library exports links to nothing, or to the
  wrong thing.** rpcss got `list_add_tail`/`list_remove` as externs copied from cabinet-rust's
  crate-internal `#[no_mangle]` copies of wine/list.h's inlines; i386 failed to link.
  `port resolve` now refuses a user-mode consensus `fn` that the module's import libraries
  (and the static libraries it links) export on NO arch, and drops such copies from an earlier
  run. On SOME arch is enough: i386's `GetWindowLongPtrW` is a user32.h macro for
  `GetWindowLongW`, and the prelude's per-arch `link_name` settles it. An SDK alias is followed
  to the end of its chain: commctrl.h's `#define SNDMSG SendMessage` names another alias, and
  eventvwr was declared an extern `SendMessage` that no DLL exports. wine/list.h itself is `winelist-rust`: `profile_derive` blocklists `struct list` in the
  island and re-exports the shared crate, and resolve imports the `list_*` helpers a crate
  calls.
- **A unit's global that the module's own header declares `extern`** (`extern CARDWINDOW
  *SolWnd;`) reaches every other unit through the ISLAND's extern declaration, so the defining
  unit must export it `#[no_mangle]` under its C name, or the other units' references are
  undefined. `port integrate` adds it (sol had 28).
- **WIRING a translated TU is already a PARTIAL COHAB FLIP, and an uncontrolled one.** The
  two-step everyone reaches for — "wire the module in now so it compiles and is lint-covered,
  flip the `.cpp` out later" — is not safe when the C++ is still live. shell32's `utils.rs`
  defines 58 `#[no_mangle]` names that `dll/win32/shell32`'s live C++ objects ALSO define as
  unmangled externs, including 16 `*_RustBridge` wrappers other Rust modules call. Wiring it
  produced **no duplicate-symbol error** — the linker resolves archive members against object
  files in a defined order and simply picks one — so 58 live entry points silently rerouted
  into Rust that had never executed. The guest booted, passed smoke on all three arches, then
  froze inside explorer's taskbar `OnCreate` (two of the captured names,
  `SHGetShellStyleHInstance` and `SHGetUserDisplayName`, sit in that path), which stopped
  `ProcessStartupItems` and therefore the kmtest sweep: `launched=0`, nothing runnable, HLT=1.
  **`scan_duplicate_symbols` does not catch this** — it models Rust definitions and
  `global_asm!` labels, not C/C++ objects, and the dangerous direction here is Rust shadowing
  C++ across the cohab boundary. Get the capture set before you
  wire anything, with `llvm-nm --defined-only` over both sides:
  `for o in build-<arch>/<module>/CMakeFiles/*.dir/*.obj; do llvm-nm --defined-only $o; done |
  awk '$2=="T"{print $3}' | grep -v '^__Z' | sed 's/^_//; s/@[0-9]*$//' | sort -u` intersected
  with the module's `#[no_mangle]` names. A non-empty intersection means wiring and flipping
  are ONE change, not two. `ORPHAN-BY-DESIGN` is the marker for a module in that state, and it
  is a GUARD, not a to-do item — the banner that says "the module is not wired yet, the .cpp is
  still the compiled implementation" is recording why it must stay that way until the flip.
- **The capture-set sweep must include the RUST STATICLIB's undefined set, not just the C++
  objects.** The recipe above intersects a TU's defined symbols with what every *object file*
  leaves undefined, and in a cohab build that is only half the link. `CFileSysBindData.cpp`
  measured 0 against the C++ objects and the true answer is 1: `IFileSystemBindData_Constructor`
  is called from `libshell32_rust.a` (`wine/pidl.rs`), which is exactly the population the
  object-file sweep skips. A false 0 here is the dangerous direction — it says "leaf, safe to
  flip" about a TU something still depends on. Add the archive to the undefined side:
  `llvm-nm --undefined-only build-<arch>/<module>/lib<module>_rust.a`. (It does not change the
  CDefView verdict — that flip linked and passed conformance on all three arches, which a
  dropped symbol could not have done — but the method as first written would not have caught
  it.)
- **An empty capture set is NECESSARY, not SUFFICIENT, and smoke is not the oracle for a
  flip.** CDefView.cpp turned out to be a link LEAF — `llvm-nm --undefined-only` over every
  object in shell32.dll (shell32.dir, dialogs/, folders/, shelldesktop, shellmenu, recyclebin)
  referenced NOTHING it defined, so the flip could not shadow anything. It still shipped a
  guest whose desktop died, and **smoke passed on all three arches in every one of those
  runs**, because the marker `shell ready` is reached before the desktop populates. The oracle
  that sees it is `vibeos-cli conformance`: `launched=0` against a 91-test baseline. Run the
  BASELINE first on an un-flipped tree — this worktree had never built the kmtest payload, so
  the first red run proved nothing until a control run on `HEAD~1` showed `launched=91`.
- **A new rlib's `#[no_mangle]` symbols are absent from the staticlib** unless reached: add the
  path dep + `extern crate` + a `#[used]` force-reference block. A Cargo dependency alone is
  not a reachability path.
- **Cross-crate `#[inline(always)]` with an `asm!` body doesn't fire at opt-level=1** — rustc
  falls back to a call against a name that has no symbol. Replicate the two-line asm in the
  consuming crate.
- **A cohab flip can drop a `.spec` export that was an obj-level ALIAS** in the flipped `.c` —
  the name appears in no `.c` file, only the `.spec`. gdi32's `GdiEntry16` aliased
  `DdSwapTextureHandles`. Re-provide it as a forwarding `#[no_mangle] extern "system" fn`,
  all-arch. Recurs across `GdiEntry1..15`.
- **The driver's OWN spec exports must be `extern "system"`** — `spec2def` emits
  `@ stdcall Foo`, so the linker wants `_Foo@N`, but translated bodies default to
  `extern "C"`. 22 Flt + 37 SSPI functions needed flipping.
- **One driver can legitimately hold two conventions** — ksecdd's vendored tomcrypt is cdecl
  while ReactOS's own `MD5Init`/`MD5Update`/`MD5Final` are NTAPI stdcall, in the same file.
  Split by *which library provides the symbol*, never one-block-one-ABI.
- **lld i386 cascades red herrings** — one real undefined makes it report unrelated `Ki*`/
  `Hal*` undefineds that vanish once the real one is fixed. Fix the obvious ones and re-link
  before chasing the weird ones.
- **`git core.ignorecase`**: a `Lib.c` → `Lib.rs` module that case-folds onto `lib.rs` blocks
  `git add` ("will not add file alias"). Rename the module.

### `raw-dylib` on a stdcall FUNCTION imports the decorated name on i386

**Symptom:** a boot driver silently missing on i386 only — FreeLDR logs `Did not find export
'RtlAssert@16'!` then `boot driver not loaded, dropped from the boot driver list`, and boot
continues without it. Every gate is green unless the boot needed that driver.

**Cause:** `#[link(name = "ntoskrnl.exe", kind = "raw-dylib", ...)] extern "system" { fn F(..); }`
makes rustc mint the import itself, and for a stdcall function on i386 it imports `F@N`; the
`.spec`-built export is the undecorated `F`. raw-dylib invents its own import descriptor, so
the link has nothing unresolved to fail on (pcix-rust's `RtlAssert`, 2026-10-10).

**Fix:** raw-dylib is for DATA exports only (`HalDispatchTable`, `InitSafeBootMode`) — a
function goes in a plain `extern "system"` block and resolves through the import library.
`scan_unresolved_imports` (binary lint, every arch) checks every livecd PE's imports against
its exporter's export table, so any name the loader cannot bind fails the build.

### Assorted ABI-adjacent traps
- **A trap handler that never sets the return register returns the caller's own argument.**
  User-mode `DbgPrint` returns what the kernel leaves in eax/rax/x0 after `int 0x2d`, and
  `KdpStub` (the no-debugger path) handled `BREAKPOINT_PRINT` without calling
  `KeSetContextReturnRegister`, so the caller got its service code back (1). Every `DPRINT1` in
  user mode then read "failed" and printed a second `(file:line) DbgPrint() failed!` line,
  doubling serial debug output. `KdpTrap` always set it; with no debugger a print succeeded.
- **`ptr & 0xFFFF0000` is not "pointer > 0xFFFF" on 64-bit.** It tests bits 16-31 only, so a
  real pointer at `...0000_xxxx` passes as a MAKEINTATOM/MAKEINTRESOURCE value. ReactOS'
  `RtlpCheckIntegerAtom` did this: whenever NtAddAtom/NtFindAtom captured a name into a pool
  block at such an address, every name became integer atom `xxxx` for the rest of the boot.
  Unrelated window properties then collided (uxtheme read shell32's `CPLFlags` value 1 as its
  WND_DATA pointer), and arm64 applets died with no window, one boot in two. Write the test as
  `p & !0xFFFF == 0` (Windows' `IS_INTRESOURCE`). The tell: atoms below 0xC000 that the atom
  table never created, with the same value across processes and a different one each boot.
  The resource walker's `find_entry_by_name` had the same test (name looked up as an id).
  `IsCallProcHandle`'s `== 0xFFFF0000` form is the same shape but was left alone: a handle
  that crossed a 32-bit LONG arrives sign-extended, and the loose test is what accepts it.
- **LLM appends `as u64` to every SIZE_T/ULONG_PTR** → ~50 i386-only E0308s. Use `as _` or
  `usize`; never hardcode a width for an arch-width field.
- **amd64 `cpuid` 32-bit `xchg ebx` dance zero-extends and wipes the upper 32 bits of rbx**,
  which is callee-saved and may hold a caller's pointer → BUGCHECK 0x50 at a truncated
  address. Use 64-bit `xchg` on amd64; cast at the return boundary, not inside the asm.
- **`PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS` is `0x001F0FFF` on NT 5.x**, not the Vista `0x001FFFFF` in
  `ntkrnl_sys::constants` — the mismatch against C-built access checks hung i386 SMSS.
  `THREAD_ALL_ACCESS` already matches.
- **`HIGH_LEVEL` is 31 on i386 but 15 on amd64/arm64**; amd64 maps IRQL to CR8 (4 valid bits),
  so `mov cr8, 0x1F` is a #GP at boot with an unreliable reported Rip. Disassemble the suspect
  HAL fn and look for `mov cr8, <imm > 15>` — trust the instruction stream over the
  symbolicator for control-register #GPs.
- **c2rust union/bitfield access vs `__BindgenUnionField`** — the repo's bindgen renders every
  union as the legacy accessor-struct, so c2rust's native `reg.All = x` / `reg.Bits.Flag()` /
  `Reg { All: 0 }` all fail (E0599/E0609/E0063). Mechanical: init → `zeroed()`, read →
  `.as_ref()`, write → `*x.as_mut() =`. Nested anon names differ (`.c2rust_unnamed` →
  `.__bindgen_anon_1`), and a member bindgen *flattened* drops the prefix entirely. A native
  bindgen `union` (ddk `_LARGE_INTEGER`) IS direct-access — grep the substrate to tell which.
- **bindgen prefixes enum constants with the enum tag** (`_SCSI_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_RequestComplete`)
  and wraps long `: <type> = N;` onto the next line. Automate: grep the substrate for
  `pub const [A-Za-z0-9_]*<name>:` (anchor the trailing colon so the wrap doesn't break it) and
  emit `pub use ... as <bare>;` — type-free `pub use` beats re-declaring a typed const.
- **Two bindgen `*-sys` crates cannot both be glob-imported** (E0659 on `BOOL`/`DWORD`/`HWND`).
  Pick one for the type bulk; declare the other's functions in local extern blocks using the
  chosen crate's types. Same for `ntkrnl_sys::base::*` + `ntkrnl_sys::ddk::*` — keep the `ddk`
  glob and import base items explicitly.
- **`src/main.rs` is auto-detected as a cargo BIN target** — a module from `main.c` collides
  with the convention and every sibling import "fails to resolve". Set `autobins = false`.
- **i386 FAST_IO / NTAPI callback slots are `extern "stdcall"`** — don't name a raw fn type;
  transmute the `extern "system"` fn item straight to the bindgen `Option<...>` slot type,
  which carries the correct per-arch ABI.

---

### A float return read through a double-typed trampoline is 0.0 on x64 and arm64

**Symptom:** a dynamic-call path (DispCallFunc, a varargs thunk) returns 0.0 for every
`float`-returning callee on amd64 only, while i386 is correct.
**Cause:** one asm trampoline serves every return type, and the caller's extern declaration
picks the register it reads. Win64 returns a `float` in xmm0's low 32 bits, so declaring the
trampoline `-> f64` reads those bits as a denormal double, and `as f32` gives 0.0. i386 hides
it because x87 `st(0)` holds either width. Wine's own `typelib.c` x86_64 path has this bug.
**Fix:** alias the trampoline under a second name declared `-> f32` (arm64's C already does:
`call_float_method`), and read float returns through it.

### `transmute(f as *const ())` into a callback slot erases the ABI check
**Symptom.** Works on amd64/arm64; on i386 the callee reads garbage arguments. In consrv this
killed csrss (BUGCHECK 0xF4) the first time an i386 GUI console was created. A BOOL slot
filled by a fn returning `u8` returns garbage upper bits on every arch.

**Cause.** `f as *const ()` discards `f`'s ABI and the transmute re-types it as the slot's
`extern "system" fn`. rustc cannot compare them. consrv's `GuiVtbl` filled 25 NTAPI slots
this way under a comment claiming the impls were `extern "system"`; 22 were plain Rust fns
and six returned `u8` for C's `BOOL`. msgina's dialog procs and advapi32's crypt callbacks
had the same shape.

**Fix.** Declare the fn with the slot's ABI and pass it directly: `Some(f)`. rustc then
checks the ABI and the whole signature. `scan_fnptr_abi_transmute` gates it (baseline empty).

### Pointer arithmetic on a field bindgen typed as an opaque stub strides one byte
**Symptom.** A table that works while only entry 0 is used. Once there are several entries
they overlap, and a pointer read back from one is garbage. consrv's console handle table
crashed csrss in `ConSrvCloseHandle` on the first console close.

**Cause.** bindgen emits an unseen type as `struct X { _address: u8 }`. A field `*mut X` makes
`.add(i)` step one byte, and the cast afterwards (`field.add(i) as PREAL`) comes too late. The
allocation used the real element size, so nothing looked wrong until index 1.

**Fix.** Cast first: `(field as PREAL).add(i)`, ideally through one helper
(`consrv/handle.rs::handle_at`). `scan_opaque_ptr_arith` gates it (baseline empty).

### A COM interface the -sys crate carries opaque has no methods and no fields
**Symptom.** `cannot find function IStream_Seek` (every widl wrapper but the ones some other
path generated) and `no field cbSize on type ntdll_sys::nt::tagSTATSTG`, though the module's
own headers define both in full. mfplat's byte stream, 57 errors deep.

**Cause.** A user-mode island blocklists every name ntdll-sys exports, so the module shares
one identity for NT types. ntdll-sys carries `IStream`, `IStreamVtbl` and `tagSTATSTG` as
`{ _unused: [u8; 0] }` (rtl's memory stream only needs the pointer), and the blocklist keeps
the empty version. No vtable means `port macros` has nothing to generate wrappers from.

**Fix.** `UNBLOCK="IStream IStreamVtbl tagSTATSTG STATSTG LPSTREAM"` in the module's `# >>> hand`
block, then re-island: the island owns the full objidl definitions. Not automatic for every
opaque name: `_TP_POOL` and friends are opaque in the real headers too, and a local copy of
those would split their identity from the ntdll-sys functions that take them.

### `(base as *mut PBYTE).offset(n)` strides by a POINTER, not a byte
The C's `(PBYTE)base + n` came out as a cast to a pointer *to* a `PBYTE` followed by
`.offset(n)`, which steps 8 bytes per unit on 64-bit; the result is cast straight back, so it
compiles everywhere and is wrong only once `n != 0`. oleaut32's `IRecordInfoImpl_RecordCopy`
read every field past offset 0 from 8x its address (Wine's vartype test died in
`SysAllocString` on the garbage BSTR); win32k's `DIB_16BPP_TransparentBlt` wrote 8x past its
destination rect (16bpp only, so the 32bpp smoke never saw it). **Gated:
`tools/scan_byteptr_stride.py`** — the tree holds no legitimate `*mut PBYTE` arithmetic.

### `(p as *mut u8).add(1)` for the C's `(PUCHAR)(p + 1)` steps one BYTE, not one struct
The reverse error: the C steps past a whole header (`p + 1`, then casts) and the Rust casts
first. usetup's cabinet reader took `(PUCHAR)(PCABHeader + 1)` as `+1` byte, read the folder
table from inside the 36-byte CFHEADER, and faulted extracting the first file; that crashed the
bootcd's smss.exe (BUGCHECK 0x71). Its `CFFILE + 1` name walk, setuplib's `NTOS_INSTALLATION + 1`
strings (written over the struct's own ListEntry) and the recycle bin's `INFO2_HEADER + 1` records
had it too. **Gated: `tools/scan_byte_step_one.py`**, baselined with the four sites where `p`
really is a byte pointer. A new hit is a site to read against its C.

### `LIST_FOR_EACH_ENTRY` translated without its container_of

**Symptom:** an access violation inside a list walk on the first call, often in a
`*ReleaseGroup*`/teardown path that boot never reaches. `rtl-threadpool`'s
`TpReleaseCleanupGroupMembers` faulted on every call, an empty group included.

**Cause:** Wine's `LIST_FOR_EACH_ENTRY(obj, head, T, field)` hides a container_of
(`LIST_ENTRY(elem, T, field)`) on both the start and the advance. The translation cast
`head.next as *mut T` directly, which is only right when `field` is at offset 0. Here it was
`group_entry`, deep in the struct, so the walk read a list node as an object and the head
check never matched. Two later loops in the same function, from the same response, had the
subtraction.

**Fix:** use `LIST_ENTRY!` (rtl-threadpool's `wine_list.rs`) or `CONTAINING_RECORD` on both
cursors. To triage, grep `\.(next|prev|Flink|Blink)\)? as \*mut <Struct>` and check the field's
offset. The 2026-09-30 sweep found 22 hits; all but this one were offset-0 (secur32's
`entry`) or were casting to a byte or void pointer.

### A switch `break` that now leaves the loop
**Symptom.** A loop over a list or an array stops after the first element of one kind.
mf's session_check_topology leaked one node reference per SetTopology (Wine's suite counted
eight); welcome's TranslateEscapes stopped translating after the first `\x`.

**Cause.** C's `case X: ...; break;` inside a `for`/`while` leaves the SWITCH. Translated to
a `match` arm ending in `break;`, it leaves the LOOP, skipping the rest of the iteration
(mf's `IMFTopologyNode_Release(node)`) and every later element.

**Fix.** Delete the `break;`: a match arm never falls through. Not the once-through
`loop { match .. }` idiom some translations use for a switch, where leaving the loop is
leaving the switch. `scan_match_arm_break` gates it; its baseline is the 19 sites
triaged as deliberate (the C had a `goto` to the function's exit, or the Rust is
hand-written).

### A list walk that starts at the head it stops at

**Symptom:** a lookup in a wine/list.h list never finds anything, or a count is always 0.
Nothing crashes. rpcss's IrotIsRunning and IrotGetObject never found a registered object.

**Cause:** `LIST_FOR_EACH_ENTRY` lowered with the cursor set to the container of `&head`
itself instead of `head->next`. The `while cursor->field != &head` test then fails before the
first iteration.

**Fix:** start at `head.next`. `scan_list_walk_from_head` (`vibeos-cli check`) flags the shape.

The opposite end matters too. In C, a walk that runs to the end leaves the cursor on the
HEAD's container, and code relies on it: `list_add_before(&ent->entry, new)` after a search
loop means "before the head", i.e. append. A macro whose cursor stops on the last node
inserts one place too early. One that rebinds the cursor per iteration (`let $elem` in the
loop, as ole32's does) leaves the caller's variable stale. winelist-rust's
`LIST_FOR_EACH_ENTRY{,_SAFE}` assign the caller's variable and finish on the head's
container, as C does. Its tests pin the append shape.

### A list walk that reads `Flink` after freeing the entry

**Symptom:** an intermittent access violation inside a list walk, at a load like
`[entry+0x28]`, with a non-canonical or misaligned pointer, e.g. arm64 FaultVA
`0x11FFFFFA80004241`. It hit kmtest RtlRangeList on all three arches about one sweep in five.
Most runs pass because freed pool still holds the old link.

**Cause:** `RemoveEntryList(Entry); Free(Container); Entry = (*Entry).Flink;`. The advance
reads freed memory, and faults only when the block was reused first. `IoCompleteRequest` counts
as a free here, because the IRP can be gone once it returns. Upstream C carries this shape in
places (`FsRtlUninitializeOplock`'s walks), and a port can predate the place upstream fixed it
(`RtlDeleteOwnersRanges`, fixed upstream in #9248).

**Fix:** capture `let next = (*entry).Flink;` at the top of the loop body, or pop from the
head (`while !IsListEmpty { RemoveHeadList }`). To triage, look in each loop for an advance
`X = (*X).Flink` preceded by a free or completion of the containing record, with no `break` or
`return` in between. The 2026-10-08 scan of `sdk/lib/rust` found 3 real hits in 13
candidates. The rest freed a different object, or stepped to `Blink` before the free.

### A C byte count kept as the element count of a `u16` copy moves twice the bytes
**Symptom.** A string copy that over-reads its source and over-writes its destination by
exactly its own length. It is silent until the over-read crosses an unmapped page. On arm64,
staging `winsxs` made smss enumerate long names and hit BUGCHECK 0x50 in `memcpy`, called
from `fastfat.sys` (`FatQueryDirectory`).

**Cause.** `RtlCopyMemory(dst, src, Bytes)` counts bytes. `core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping`
counts elements of `T`, and `T` is whatever the pointers say. The translation kept
`BytesConverted` and typed the pointers `u16`. The same shape was in the registry value cache
(uncompressed value names) and in five mountmgr `DeviceString` copies, plus one uncast
instance in `IoVolumeDeviceToDosName`.

**Fix.** Copy bytes as the C does (`src as *const u8, dst as *mut u8, Bytes`), or divide the
count by `size_of::<u16>()`. Keep element-typed pointer arithmetic for the destination
offset: `&Dst[Len / sizeof(WCHAR)]` is `dst.add(len / 2) as *mut u8`.
`scan_wide_byte_copy` gates the cast form (baseline empty). It only trusts an explicit cast,
because both pointers share one `T`, and an uncast `.Buffer` is too often ANSI. An uncast
`u16` field pair still needs reading against the C.
**Any element type, and `as *const _` hides it.** partmgr's `FdoIoctlDiskGetDriveLayoutEx`
copied `copy_nonoverlapping(layoutEx as *const _, SystemBuffer as *mut _, size)`: `_` inferred
`DRIVE_LAYOUT_INFORMATION_EX` (192 bytes), so every `IOCTL_DISK_GET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX` wrote
size × 192 bytes (~117 KB) through a 624-byte system buffer: BUGCHECK 0x19 `BAD_POOL_HEADER`
next to an `IOBU` block. Smoke never sends that IOCTL; the first program that did (diskpart,
under the `modrun` payload) bugchecked. The disassembly says it outright (`shl $6; lea
(%rax,%rax,2)` before `memcpy`). `scan_typed_byte_copy` gates the general form: an explicit
non-byte cast, or `_` resolved through the source variable's declared type, with a byte-named
count or one multiplied by `size_of` (baseline empty).
**And the ORDER flips too.** `RtlMoveMemory(dst, src, bytes)` is destination-first;
`core::ptr::copy(src, dst, count)` is source-first. imm32's `Imm32FixLogFont` translated both
of its face-name shifts with the C's argument order and the C's byte count, so each moved the
string the wrong way by twice its length (`scan_silent_failures` caught the `size_of` count;
nothing catches the order). Read every `copy`/`copy_nonoverlapping` against its C call.

## LLVM folds: ud2, captures(none), and the CGU lottery

> **2026-07-05 status:** the volatile-blind attribute-deduction root is **fixed in the shipping
> toolchains** (LLVM 21.1.3+: volatile stores block `readnone captures(none)`; plain out-writes
> deduce fold-proof `writeonly initializes(...)`). A post-opt IR audit of the amd64 kernel found
> **zero live folds**. Layout-robustness is proven empirically: `VIBEOS_LAYOUT_CANARY=1`
> (451 symbols relocated) booted 5/5, where the 2026-06 tree deterministically 0x50'd. The
> **ABI-mismatch → ud2 cascade above is toolchain-independent and fully live.** Keep
> `tools/audit-captures.sh <arch>` in the loop after every rustc/LLVM bump; the entries below
> matter the day a bump regresses it.

### Triage order for any named-function `ud2` `[§9.103]`
1. `scan_ir_mismatch` the crate — CC/signature mismatch is the overwhelming majority.
2. Then the **provable-null-deref fold**, which survives every CC fix and is *not* a mismatch:
   in release builds LLVM sees through a same-crate callee, proves a deref is null, and folds.
   Two sources — **DUMMY_PSEH eager filter evaluation** (cdfs `CdPerformVerify`) and
   **unguarded C null-blindness** (win32k `UserRedrawDesktop`), where the C "works" only
   because nothing ever passes null.
3. Only then captures(none).

### The i386 driver-fleet ud2-bomb class `[§9.99]`
Any same-LLVM-module disagreement about one symbol folds and **passes the linker**. `scan_ud2`
was ntoskrnl-only, so a whole driver fleet carried live bombs. The five shapes:
`#[link_name]` redirects that don't match; a local shim def vs the bindgen decl class; a
`#[no_mangle]` with **no** `extern "…"` (raw symbol, Rust ABI); fastcall decls over cdecl defs
(the kernel exports `Interlocked*` FASTCALL on i386); variadic decls over a non-variadic def.
`cdrom.sys` carried **100** ud2 sites, all on paths boot never hits — which is exactly why
master was green.

**A sixth shape does not fold at all: two DECLARATIONS, no definition.** fastfat's
`fileinfo.rs` declared the cdecl cohab thunk `IoGetCurrentIrpStackLocation` as `"system"` while
`cachesup`/`create`/`dirctrl` said `"C"`. rustc keeps one declaration per symbol per crate, so
fileinfo's call bound to `_IoGetCurrentIrpStackLocation` (cdecl, caller pops) but was compiled
with stdcall's bookkeeping (callee pops): `push; call` and no `add esp`, then locals read at
offsets that assume the pop. `esp` came back 4 bytes off and the next esp-relative load read a
garbage pointer: i386 BUGCHECK 0x50, P1 nonsense, in a closure body right after the helper
call, only when notepad saved a file to FAT. The tell in the disassembly is a cdecl call with
no stack cleanup. `scan_cc_mismatch` reports it as `[DECL_CC_SPLIT]` (it needs no in-crate
definition: two answers to one question are already wrong).

One of the two "declarations" need not be an `extern` block in the crate. A `use
ntkrnl_sys::ddk::{.., IoCopyCurrentIrpStackLocationToNext, ..}` brings bindgen's cdecl one in,
and rustc merges it with a local `"system"` copy just the same. That was fastfat's flush.rs,
in the very block where the fileinfo fix had moved `IoGetCurrentIrpStackLocation` to `"C"`;
pnp.rs imported the helper from the ddk. The call sat in `FatCommonFlushBuffers`' finally, whose
epilogue is esp-based (`add esp; pop esi/edi/ebx/ebp; ret`), so the 4-byte leak popped every
saved register one slot off and `ret` jumped INTO THE STACK. Each crash looked different (0x23
"unexpected exception at a stack address", 0x50, 0x1E, 0x7F), and all of them came at the first
`NtFlushBuffersFile` on a writable FAT root (eventlog opening AppEvent.Evt). With EIP on the stack, the
word at the faulting esp names whatever was just pushed or returned through; disassemble the
function it points into and look for a call with no stack cleanup. The scanner now counts
named `-sys` imports and qualified `x_sys::..::F(` calls as declarations.

**Not every unexpected `ud2` is this class — `scan_ud2` reports all of them under it. Read the
instruction BEFORE the trap first; it names the cause in one look.**

| Preceding instruction | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `call …panic_bounds_check` | array index the optimiser can't prove in range (see the indexing-panic entry) | pointer arithmetic at the unprovable site only |
| `int $0x29` | `__fastfail` (`RtlFailFast`): the LIST_ENTRY integrity check in `RemoveEntryList`/`RemoveHeadList`, as in the C header inline. Expected; `scan_ud2` classifies it so since 2026-10-08 (atapi.sys showed 9) | none |
| `call` to an ordinary function, no panic symbol | LLVM folded a UB path to `unreachable` after inlining | below |
| none of the above | a genuine CC/sig-mismatch fold — the five shapes above | fix the ABI disagreement |

The middle row is the subtle one, and msvcrt's file.c hit **both** it and the bounds-check row in
the same build. Shape: a callee that can return NULL, inlined into a caller that dereferences the
result unchecked. LLVM sees NULL reach a deref, concludes UB, and emits `unreachable` — which
lands as `call <whatever ran last>` then `ud2`, *one per calling function*, so the trap appears
in callers that contain no such code. `msvcrt_get_file` returns NULL on `calloc` failure and
`_fcloseall`/`_rmtmp`/`msvcrt_flush_all_buffers` all do `file->_flag` straight away — **which is
precisely what the C does.** The tell that you are in this row rather than the CC row is that
the ud2 count tracks the number of *callers*, and the C source has the same missing check.

**Making a silent debug macro real is a trigger for this row, and the trap is not a
regression.** Burning down the no-op `ERR`/`FIXME` macros put two `ud2` in `user32.dll`
(`GetScrollPos`, `GetScrollRange`) that master did not have. `IntGetSBData` returns NULL on two
arms and every caller derefs the result unchecked — *which is what `scrollbar.c` does*. While
`ERR` expanded to nothing, LLVM had no side effect to keep and deleted the whole branch, so the
UB was invisible; an opaque `DbgPrint` call must be kept, the NULL now visibly reaches a deref,
and the tail folds. Same fix, same reasoning as below. The general point: an empty debug macro
is not merely a lost message, it is also **an optimiser hint that erases the evidence** — so
expect this class when you turn one on, and read the trap as a pre-existing latent fold rather
than as damage the change did.

**DELETING code is the same trigger, from the other direction.** Reverting upstream's
`TIF_MOVESIZETRACKING` hack out of `ENTRY_ReferenceEntryByHandle` (win32k `gdiobj.rs`) put one
`ud2` in `win32k.sys` at `EBRUSHOBJ_bRealizeBrush` that the previous build did not have. Nothing
about that function changed; the removal simply made `ENTRY_ReferenceEntryByHandle` small enough
to inline, which made `GDIOBJ_ShareLockObj` transparent at its call site, and
`engbrush.rs`'s `psurfPattern = GDIOBJ_ShareLockObj(...)` is dereferenced with no NULL check --
*which is what the C does*, since `engbrush.c` carries only `ASSERT(psurfPattern)` and ASSERT is
nothing in retail. So: **any edit that changes a function's INLINING COST can uncloak this row,
including one that only removes lines.** Read the instruction before the trap
(`call GDIOBJ_vDereferenceObject`, an ordinary function with no panic symbol = middle row), fix
with `#[inline(never)]` on the NULL-returning callee, and do not add the null check.

**Fix by restoring the C's codegen shape — `#[inline(never)]` on the callee — not by adding the
null check.** Adding it is a behaviour change on the path the C would fault on, i.e. a
divergence in a differential port; out-of-line, the caller gets an opaque pointer, emits the
ordinary load, and faults exactly where C faults. Confirm the latent path is unreachable anyway
before you accept it (in msvcrt's case every caller walks `3..MSVCRT_stream_idx`, and those slots
are allocated at stream-creation time, so the `calloc` arm is never reached with such an index) —
and if it *is* reachable, you have found a real bug in the C and should say so rather than
silence the trap.

### Making a no-op opaque UNCLOAKS everything hiding behind the fold
A C debug macro that expands to nothing, translated as a no-op **`fn`**, is trivially inlinable
— LLVM folds it away *with every argument expression*, and with them any relocation reachable
only through those arguments. Give it an out-of-line body (e.g. a C variadic trampoline) and
the latents materialise at once: undefined symbols for ABI-mismatched callees, `extern static`
decls for what are C `#define`s, and a fresh ud2 cascade. cdrom went 100 → 114 ud2, one on a
live path → i386 BUGCHECK 0x1E `0xC000001D` after `calll _TracePrint`. **The errors point at
innocent code.** Fix: make it a `macro_rules!` (the faithful shape — C never evaluates the
args), consume args by value (`let _ = $arg;`; `&$arg` is E0793 on a packed field), and do
**not** type-bind the parameters, because the per-module extern decls it replaces routinely
disagree with each other. Then fix the ABI mismatches you uncovered — they are real.
The other face of the same trap: once the no-op is out of line, its arguments **run**, and they
are reads the C never performs. usbport's `USBPORT_QueueTransferUrb` ends by dumping
`*Urb->TransferBuffer` through `DPRINT_URB` after the URB is queued; with the drvtrace-shim
no-op symbols that loop executed, and on two CPUs the transfer had already completed on the
other one, so it read a NULL `TransferBuffer` at DISPATCH_LEVEL. Symptom far from the cause: a
paging read failing `d0000006`/`c0000001` in cdfs (whose try/except swallowed the in-page
exception), on half of amd64-bios `-smp 2` boots. `scan_macro_fn_shadow` now harvests every
argument-discarding C macro (`if(0)`, `__noop`, `(void)0`) from the headers and flags an empty
Rust fn of that name in any crate, a shim crate included. Expect the conversion itself to
uncloak something: with the opaque call gone, usbehci's `EHCI_AllocTd` inlined into
`EHCI_OpenInterruptEndpoint`, whose unchecked deref of its NULL return (a C bug) became a
`scan_ud2` failure. Fix the uncloaked bug; don't restore the barrier.
The same bug also comes as an `extern` DECLARATION, `extern "C" { fn TRACE(fmt: *const i8, ...); }`,
bound at link time to whatever no-op some crate or cohab stub happens to export. That form has
no body for the empty-fn check to see. By 2026-10-10 that had hidden about 386 NT_ASSERT calls in
five storage/FS drivers, plus 93 declarations of Wine TRACE/ERR, DPRINT, KdPrintEx and similar.
fastfat's NT_ASSERT evaluated an operand that faults (cachesup.rs). `scan_macro_fn_shadow` flags these declarations now too. Convert with
`tools/fn_call_to_macro.py`. When you write the replacement macro, never name it after a std
macro: a crate-root `macro_rules! assert` shadows `core::assert!` in every module declared
after it. cabinet's compile-time `FDINOTIFICATION` layout asserts silently became no-ops that
way, and they still compiled.
A third form is a C stub DEFINITION in the module's own cohab file. fastfat's fatdata.h
`DebugTrace`/`DebugUnwind`/`DebugDump`/`DbgDoit` are `{NOTHING;}` in a free build. The Rust
called them as FFI into `VOID DebugTrace(...) {}` bodies in rust_cohab_stub.c, about 880 calls
(fixed 2026-10-11: crate macros that discard their tokens). `scan_macro_fn_shadow` did not
flag them, so check why its harvest misses a driver-private header like fatdata.h.

### A C macro that NULLS its argument, translated as a by-value `fn`, silently double-frees
Symptom: 0x19 BAD_POOL_HEADER "at the next free" (special pool escalates it to 0x1E in a pool
routine, e.g. `ExReturnPoolQuota`); the free-list dump shows one pointer freed twice back to
back. Cause: a C free-and-null macro — classpnp/cdrom `FREE_POOL` is
`#define FREE_POOL(p) { ExFreePool(p); p = NULL; }` — was translated as
`extern "C" fn FREE_POOL(ptr: *mut c_void)`. A fn takes the pointer by value and **cannot null
the caller's local**, so the macro's NULL side effect is dropped. Any site that frees in a
branch/loop and then again at a cleanup label double-frees, because the C relied on that NULL
to make the second `if (p) FREE_POOL(p)` a no-op. cdrom's `DeviceSetRawReadInfo` hit it (and
the translation compounded it by *adding* a `FREE_POOL(buffer)` in a success branch where the
C just `break`s to a single FnExit free). Fix at the site: null the local after each free,
matching the macro (`p = core::ptr::null_mut();`); fix generally: make `FREE_POOL` a
`macro_rules!` that nulls, but note call sites passing `p as *mut c_void` can't be nulled
through the cast, so the macro must take the bare variable. Same shape as the no-op-macro-as-fn
entries above: a C macro's *semantics* (here a side effect, there lazy arg evaluation) do not
survive being made a fn — check for side effects on the arguments before lowering a macro to a fn.
Scope of the class (audited 2026-10-08, cdrom-rust + classpnp-rust + disk-rust, $0): it is far
rarer than it looks. `DeviceSetRawReadInfo` was the *only* real instance in the whole storage
stack. Detection heuristic (cheap static scan): within each fn, group `FREE_POOL`/`FREE_POOL!`
calls by their exact freed lvalue and flag a same-pointer pair only when NO
`return`/`break`/`continue`/reassignment/null-set sits between them. Nearly every raw hit is a
false positive — the translator mirrors the C control flow, so the two frees live in
mutually-exclusive `match` arms, on either side of a `break 'switch`/`continue 'retry`, or the
"use after free" is a pointer-*value* compare evaluated before the free. classpnp's
`ClassDeviceControl` alone threw 52 such false hits. The blanket `macro_rules!`-that-nulls
migration was considered and rejected: ~100 call sites would need the `FREE_POOL!` form, cast
stripping, and assignable lvalues, to fix zero live bugs. Audit per site; don't migrate.

### NEVER hand-write `memcpy`/`memset`/`memmove`/`memcmp` in Rust `[§9.65]`
**It cannot be done correctly.** LLVM folds any byte-copy loop back into a call to the function
itself → **infinite self-recursion**. (The one place the tree does implement them, cnt-rust's
exports, does it in inline asm for exactly this reason: `cabi/memops.rs`.) The PC parks on a literal `jmp .` and the serial log is
empty. `ntoskrnl.exe` exports all of them on every arch — **import them, don't define them.**

This is the other **cloak** bug: `-Z build-std-features=compiler-builtins-mem` had been linking
the real implementations ahead of a broken hand-written one in bootvid **for months**, so
dropping `-Z build-std` for the builtin triples made both amd64 and arm64 hang at boot with a
completely empty serial log. A real defect held harmless by a link-order accident — exactly the
same shape as the no-op-fn fold above, and the reason a "no functional change" toolchain edit
can detonate.

**A second route to the same `jmp .`, and this one is invisible in the source: a `#[no_mangle]`
export whose body calls an `extern` declaration carrying `#[link_name = "<that same export>"]`.**
Two different Rust identifiers, no recursion anywhere on the page, and the loop only exists
after the linker resolves both to one symbol. Seen 2026-08-04 in a `drvdefext.cpp` flip: the
model needed `SH_FormatByteSize`, which is C++-linkage in a *different* TU
(`dialogs/filedefext.cpp`) and only reachable through `drvdefext.cpp`'s own
`SH_FormatByteSize_RustBridge` forwarder — so it imported the bridge under that `link_name` and
then also published a `#[no_mangle]` bridge of the same name that called it. `cargo check` is
perfectly happy. `scan_self_recursive` does catch it, but only post-link, and a duplicate-symbol
error would usually fire first. **Rule: when a flip needs a `*_RustBridge` forwarder, the
forwarder belongs in the TU that OWNS the target function, not in the TU being flipped away.**
Grep a new module for any name that appears both as a `link_name` and as a `#[no_mangle]` fn.

**A third route, shorter than both: an `extern` block *inside* the `#[no_mangle] fn` that
redeclares the very name the fn defines.** `#[no_mangle] fn KeRaiseIrql(..) { extern "system"
{ fn KeRaiseIrql(..); } KeRaiseIrql(..) }` reads as "forward to the real export", and is not:
a local strong definition beats an importlib thunk, so the call binds to the enclosing
function. classpnp shipped three of these — `KeRaiseIrql`, `KeLowerIrql`,
`IoWMIDeviceObjectToProviderId` — as literal two-byte infinite loops
(`4fb90 <KeRaiseIrql>: eb fe  jmp 4fb90`), spinning any storage path that touched IRQL with no
bugcheck and no serial output. **A shim is only ever needed on the arch that has NO export**,
so the fix is per-arch `cfg`, not a forwarding body: check `hal.spec` / `ntoskrnl.spec` for the
`-arch=` list before writing one. Here i386 wanted the FASTCALL `KfRaiseIrql` decoration,
amd64 wanted real CR8 bodies for both, and arm64 wanted no definition at all.

**And the `-arch=` list is only half the check — `-private` decides whether you can LINK it.**
`ntoskrnl.spec:635` really does export `KeLowerIrql` on amd64, but as
`@ cdecl -arch=x86_64 -private KeLowerIrql(long) KxLowerIrql`, and `spec2def.c:750` keeps
private exports out of the *import library*: the symbol is in the DLL and unreachable from a
driver. Dropping the shim on that reading cost a `ld.lld: error: undefined symbol:
KeLowerIrql`. So the real question a shim answers is not "does the OS export this" but "is
there an importlib entry" — grep the spec line for `-private` before deleting a definition.
**A `#[no_mangle]` shim that
mentions its own name in an `extern` block is always this bug** — and note the shape survives
`cargo check`, `clippy` and code review, and is only visible post-link.

**The quiet version is a stub that links and returns nothing.** Instead of a loop, the shim
satisfies an unresolved name with `{ core::ptr::null_mut() }`. That boots, so nothing flags it.
classpnp carried `RtlInterlockedPushEntrySList`/`PopEntrySList` stubs from 2026-06-10 to
2026-10-07: ntkrnl-sys binds the SList pair to those `Rtl` names, which only exist inside
ntoskrnl (drivers must import `ExpInterlocked*` on 64-bit, FASTCALL `Interlocked*` on i386,
`ntoskrnl.spec:175-176,327-328`). Every free-list push dropped its packet and every pop came
back empty, so each disk request allocated a fresh transfer packet and SRB and leaked them,
including through ntkrnl-sys's inline lookaside helpers. The symptom was not "out of memory":
amd64-bios boots failed paging reads with `STATUS_IN_PAGE_ERROR` (C0000006) in 15 of 80 runs,
and none in 16 runs after the shims forwarded to the real exports. The failure mechanism was
not pinned down. Check: `objdump -p <driver>.sys | grep <name>` must show an IMPORT, and
`objdump -d` of a shim must show a `jmp` to that import, not `xor eax,eax; ret`.
`tools/scan_export_shadows.py` (in `vibeos-cli check`) finds the class from source: a
kernel-mode driver crate defining a name ntoskrnl.spec or hal.spec exports, or the internal
name an export forwards to (the column classpnp's stubs were named after). Its first run also
found kdgdb defining its own `KdComPortInUse`, a HAL *data* export, so the HAL never learned
the debug port was taken, and four drivers whose empty `RtlAssert` hid every failed ASSERT.
A data export must be imported through `#[link(kind = "raw-dylib")]`, never defined.

### captures(none)-class hardening that is still worth doing
- **Stale/hoisted load through a `static mut` table across a foreign call** — a by-handle
  lookup wrongly rejects an object; a `DbgPrint` between the reads "fixes" it. `read_volatile`
  at the reads, `write_volatile` at the paired writes. Proven pre-emptive step for any win32k
  handle/object/refcount table; boot-time single-threaded init never exercises it.
- **MMIO needs volatile too.** A type error on `write_volatile(cfg.add(0), WIDE_CONST)` gets
  "fixed" as `*cfg.offset(0) = WIDE_CONST as u8`, silently dropping volatile → the driver
  enumerates garbage. **Cast the value, keep volatile.** After any MMIO-touching driver, diff
  `grep -c volatile` before/after.
- **Shared clock reads in spin-waits need volatile** — a `do {} while (t0 == t1)` calibration
  loop never sees the tick change because LLVM hoists the non-volatile load out. i386 was
  immune (it called the real export). Any fixed-VA shared page used as a polling condition.
- **Non-volatile seqlock loops on KUSER_SHARED_DATA are the arm64 `b .` spin class** `[§9.106]`
  — the KSYSTEM_TIME capture loop with plain loads becomes an infinite self-branch (kernel32
  time functions, `EngInitializeSafeSemaphore`). The writer protocol (High1, Low, High2) is the
  same class. Grep any `High1Time`/`High2Time`/SharedUserData access for volatility.
- **`#[no_mangle]` alone does not stop inlining** — it preserves the symbol; LLVM can still
  inline the body into a same-CGU caller. The `#[inline(never)]` set on `shim_exports.rs` is
  defence-in-depth, not redundancy.
- **Don't wrap a *written* `#[no_mangle] pub static` in `Volatile<T>`** — a non-`mut` static
  can land in `.rdata` and page-fault on write despite interior mutability. Keep `static mut`
  and use volatile accessors.
- **Re-probe old C-shim workarounds before keeping them.** Most dissolved under the
  `lto=false` + `codegen-units=256` firewall; their comments are stale. Must-stays: amd64
  `KiSaveXState`/`KiRestoreXState` (KVM bug), i386 `SepInitTokensShim` (fat-LTO ud2).
- **Trace the full consumer chain before believing "load-bearing tracing"** — a capture chain
  whose only reader has no callers is dead; delete writer, reader and callers together.

### The CGU lottery
`codegen-units=256` partitioning is **not deterministic across workspace shape**, so a body
containing a parked ud2 can move onto a live caller's path with no source change.
- **Adding a workspace member repartitions unrelated crates** → a "crp regression" that is
  really a reshuffle. Reproduce on the real tree, deep-nuked (all five `rust-*-target/` plus
  every artifact — conftest nukes only one of five) before accepting the claim.
- **Parallel cold builds → false HANG at `[freeldr] Switching stack...`** with zero kernel
  serial. That line precedes the jump to `KiSystemStartup`, a `KNOWN_CGU_UD2` function; under
  memory pressure from three concurrent cold cargo builds the partitioner lands a ud2 on the
  early-boot path. **Build cold one arch at a time** (smokes may run parallel). Escalate only
  if it reproduces solo and deterministically.
- **A monolithic CGU causes lld `X was replaced`** (distinct from the benign
  `--allow-multiple-definition` warning): all ~100 CRT shims in one module = one object, so
  referencing any symbol drags strong defs that collide with ntoskrnl imports. C had one
  `.obj` per function. Fix: wrap each generated shim in its own `mod`, restoring per-function
  CGU granularity. A 1-second relink "FAIL" is a relink against a **stale** `.a` — `ar` never
  prunes.
- **`-C no-prepopulate-passes` is the class-guard for tiny one-shim-per-CGU objects** — i386
  always carried it; amd64/arm64 (and any cargo driver that scrubs RUSTFLAGS) did not, which is
  why `libcntpr` CRT shims misbehaved *only* on 64-bit (memset dead-store-eliminated into a
  guard-only spin; `_strnicmp` collapsed to always-equal). Scope it to the offending crate,
  not the whole kernel body.
---

### A kernel object initialized in a `MaybeUninit`, then moved out with `assume_init()`
**Symptom:** 0x109 (or a garbage-thread unwait) the first time an event is SIGNALED, not when
it is waited on. The waitdep check names a "thread" that is a user-mode-looking value, and
`[KX-UNWAIT]` shows the event's wait list pointing at a self-linked entry a few bytes away.
**Cause:** `KeInitializeEvent(Event.as_mut_ptr(), ..); let Event = Event.assume_init();`
copies the object. An initialized KEVENT's empty wait list points at ITSELF, as do list heads,
KTIMER, KMUTANT, KSEMAPHORE and ERESOURCE. The copy's list still points at the old slot, so it
looks non-empty, and `KeSetEvent` unwaits whatever bytes are there. `IoShutdownSystem` did this
with its shutdown-IRP event, and mountmgr's completion bugchecked at the end of every install.
Whether the copy survives is up to the optimizer: pcix's capabilities query had the same code
and never fired. The same move hides in a constructor: `fn new_request() -> Req { let mut r =
..; KeInitializeEvent(&mut r.done, ..); r }` hands the caller a copy. NtCancelIoFileEx shipped
that way into its first guest run (0x109 on i386, 0xA on amd64, the first time it waited).
**Fix:** declare the object (`let mut E: KEVENT = zeroed();`), initialize it in place at its
final address and pass `&mut E` from then on. `tools/scan_init_then_move.py` gates both shapes
at zero.

## bindgen, struct layout & literal width

Bugs that compile and link clean but corrupt memory or strings at runtime, because the Rust
mirror, literal width, or field offset silently disagrees with C.

### Never hand-roll a shadow struct for a type bindgen already emits
The single highest-yield rule in this section. Hand-rolled mirrors drift; bindgen's are
size-verified. Real damage:
- **`#[repr(C, packed)]` on a naturally-aligned C struct** mislocates every field after the
  first alignment hole. `TDI_ADDRESS_IP { USHORT sin_port; ULONG in_addr; }` has 2 bytes of
  padding, so `in_addr` is at offset 4; a packed mirror puts it at 2 and a connect to
  10.0.2.100 parses as 2.100.0.0. The kernel's parser was right all along.
- **Five+ hand-rolled `KUSER_SHARED_DATA` shadows with fantasy offsets** → BUGCHECK 0x4C on the
  first `-smp 2` boot.
- **A per-file mini-mirror placing a field at offset 0** clobbers the real struct;
  `type X = c_void` makes `size_of::<X>() == 0` → a zero-byte allocation.
- **A GENERATED fallback mirror shadows the real port silently.** The cpp-com support block
  emits local `CStringW` / `CComHeapPtr` when it sees those names, and a local `pub struct`
  beats a prelude glob with no warning at either site. In shell32's CDefaultContextMenu that
  hid `crate::atl`'s ports, whose methods the translated bodies call — but the layout is the
  real damage: the fallback `CStringW` is a 3-word `{buffer,len,capacity}` where ATL's is ONE
  pointer, and `StaticShellEntry` is `#[repr(C)]` with a `CStringW Verb` field, so the shadow
  silently re-laid-out a struct that has to match C++. Delete the fallbacks after every
  re-assembly; the missing-method errors are the *symptom*, not the bug.
- **A whole PRIVATE SUBSTRATE, not one struct — and a FALLING error count hides it.** shell32's
  CDefView came back carrying 27 of its own substrate types: 15 SDK layouts the bindgen island
  already owns (`LVITEMW`, `LVHITTESTINFO`, `CMINVOKECOMMANDINFOEX`, `SFV_CREATE`, …) and 12 COM
  interfaces `shellcom` owns (`IUnknown`, `IStream`, `IDataObject`, `IBindCtx`, `IFolderView`
  and their vtables). Every call site in the file typechecked — against the file's OWN copies —
  so the module looked further along than it was, and only errors at its boundary with the rest
  of the crate were visible at all. Deleting them fixed ~40 errors and SURFACED ~35 the copies
  had been hiding, so the total barely moved: **the error count was the misleading number the
  whole time, and a translated TU that compiles suspiciously well is the symptom.** This is the
  whole-substrate form of the single-struct rule above, and of AGENTS.md's rule that an
  unresolved substrate name makes the model invent a forward declaration that compiles and is
  silently wrong. Detection is cheap and worth running on every fresh `--cpp-com` output: list
  the TU's top-level `pub struct`/`pub type` and intersect with the island's and with the
  crate's shared COM module. Diff each hit field-by-field before deleting — here every
  difference was spelling (`i32` vs `c_int`, `[T; 1]` vs `[T; 1usize]`) or the island being
  STRONGER (`SFV_CREATE.psvOuter` is `*mut IShellView` there and `*mut c_void` in the copy) —
  and for a vtable compare slot ORDER and ARITY first, because a slot resolves by NAME at the
  call site, so a misplaced one compiles perfectly and calls the wrong method.
- **Pin every mirror you must keep** with an arch-gated `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<T>()
  == 0xNNNN);` matching the C's `C_ASSERT` (basesrv `BASE_STATIC_SERVER_DATA` == 0x1AC8 on
  i386). Never feed a helper a pointer to a private mirror — pass
  `addr_of_mut!((*real).Field)`.
- **`FX_SAVE_AREA`** `[§9.25]`: the C `_FXSAVE_FORMAT` is **520** bytes, not 512 (trailing member); four
  hand-rolled copies modelled it as 512 → garbage `Cr0NpxState` → 0x7F GP in
  `KiFlushNPXState`.
- **A dropped term in a hand-derived `sizeof` `#define`** under-allocates and overlaps the
  extension layout; **a dropped `FIELD_OFFSET(T, Array[N])` subscript scaling** under-allocates
  the heap block.

### A `pshpack` region translated as plain `repr(C)`
**Symptom.** A file-format reader rejects valid input or reads fields a few bytes off.
oleaut32's `OleLoadPictureEx` failed every placeable metafile (Wine's olepicture `test_apm`,
then a crash on the NULL picture), and every icon directory entry was read 2 bytes late.
**Cause.** The C declared `APM_HEADER`, `CURSORICONFILEDIRENTRY` and `CURSORICONFILEDIR`
between `#include "pshpack1.h"` and `poppack.h`; the translation gave them plain `#[repr(C)]`,
so `APM_HEADER` padded to 24 bytes instead of 22 and `idEntries` moved from offset 6 to 8.
The pack pragma is invisible at the struct, so nothing at the definition looked wrong.
**Fix.** `#[repr(C, packed)]` plus a `const _: () = assert!(size_of / offset_of ...)` per
struct. Audit a module by listing every struct inside a `pshpack`/`poppack` pair in its C and
checking the Rust `repr` (a ten-line script; ole32/oleaut32's other twenty were fine). This is
the mirror image of the packed-`TDI_ADDRESS_IP` bullet above: wrong in either direction, and
only a size assert catches it.
**The pack can live in a PUBLIC header, where the module's own C never shows it.** cabinet's
hand-declared `FDINOTIFICATION` was plain `repr(C)`, but `fdi.h` wraps it in `pshpack4`: on
64-bit `pv` is at 0x1c, not 0x20, so every C client's `pfdin->pv` read half of `psz3` and half
of `pv`. i386 was right by accident (pointers are 4 bytes, so pack 4 changes nothing), which is
why the bug only surfaced on amd64/arm64 -- rapps crashed extracting its database. A
module-local audit misses this; measure the header with the module's real flags (borrow its
line from `compile_commands.json`, add `-fsyntax-only` and a `char (*x)[offsetof(T,f)+1000] = 1;`
probe, read the numbers off the diagnostics) and pin the result with `offset_of!` asserts.
**The other direction, at island scale: a pack PUSH copied into a bindgen wrapper.**
profile_derive mirrors each TU's include prologue into the module's merged `WRAPPER_INC`, and
partlist.c's prologue ENDS with `#include <pshpack1.h>` -- its `poppack.h` comes after two
typedefs. Every header after it in setuplib's wrapper was bindgen'd under pack(1): 62 structs
`#[repr(C, packed)]` that C lays out naturally, `USETUP_DATA` and the `STORAGE_*` IOCTL buffers
among them. The tell was rustc E0793 ("reference to packed field") on a struct nobody packs.
`scan_preamble` now never carries a packing include or `#pragma pack` into a wrapper; count
`repr(C, packed)` in a fresh island against the C's own pshpack regions.
**A sector layout read through it reads PAST the sector.** diskpart's `partlist.c` declares
`PARTITION` and `PARTITION_SECTOR` under `pshpack1`; the port made them plain `repr(C)`, so the
partition table moved from byte 446 to 448 and `Magic` was read at 512..514 of a 512-byte
heap buffer. No disk ever had `0xAA55` there, so every disk listed as unpartitioned ("There are
no partitions on this disk", all space free). The `modrun` C oracle showed it as a one-line
diff; the debug trace differed by one missing `Use megabyte alignment!` line.

### A `pack(N)` struct holding an aligned member has no Rust spelling (E0587 / E0588)
**Symptom.** A bindgen island fails to compile: `type has conflicting packed and align
representation hints` or `packed type cannot transitively contain a #[repr(align)] type`.
drwtsn32's amd64 island, from dbghelp.h's `MINIDUMP_THREAD_CALLBACK` (pack(4), holds a
`CONTEXT`, which is `align(16)` on amd64) and everything that holds one.
**Cause.** Legal C: MSVC lets the member's declared alignment win over the pack pragma. Rust
cannot express a packed struct whose field demands more alignment, so bindgen's faithful
output is rejected.
**Fix.** Automatic: `gen_driver_types.sh` runs `tools/rustconv/bindgen_repr_conflicts.py` on
the raw island and re-runs bindgen with those types `--opaque-type` (to a fixpoint: an opaque
replacement keeps its `align(N)`, so its packed holders are the next round). Size and
alignment stay exactly clang's; only the field layout goes. A module that needs the FIELDS of
such a type must hand-lay it out; none so far does (drwtsn32 only passes them by pointer).

### A macro translated from the wrong side of an `#ifdef`
**Symptom.** Values built through one helper are corrupt in a way that looks like two fields
swapped. In oleaut32 every negative `DECIMAL` made with `SIGNSCALE` had scale 128, and
`DECIMAL` products, quotients and `VarDecFromR8` results came back with sign and scale crossed
(Wine's vartest: `VarMul ... 0.000000, expected 46.200000`).
**Cause.** `variant.h` defines `SIGNSCALE` twice, under `#ifdef WORDS_BIGENDIAN` and `#else`;
the translation copied the big-endian branch, `(scale << 8) | sign`, and even labelled it "LE
branch". The same swap was then written inline in `VARIANT_DecFromDI`, and a reader tested the
sign as `signscale & 0x80` (bit 7 of the scale byte).
**Fix.** Use the named union fields (`scale`, `sign`) instead of composing the packed word, and
when a macro has endian or arch branches, check which one the comment claims against the
header itself. Grep the crate for every other composition of the same word.

A function BODY can take the wrong arm too. fmifs's `Chkdsk` came back with the `#else`
`GetVolumeNameForVolumeMountPointW` lookup where the live `#ifdef __REACTOS__` arm is a plain
`wcscpy`. The translate audit flags these (`PREPROCESSOR ARMS ... the #if arm is LIVE`), so
read every such finding against the Rust before flipping.

The arm can also be the wrong TARGET's. cscript compiles wscript's three `.c` with
`-DCSCRIPT_BUILD`, and every rustconv reader of `compile_commands.json` took the first entry
naming a file, so wscript-rust was translated from cscript's preprocess. It shipped
non-interactive (`wshInteractive = VARIANT_FALSE`) and printed "Usage: CScript". The
translate audit cannot see this, because the arm it took IS live, for the other target.
`macro_authority.pick_entry` now takes the ported target's entry (port sets it from
state.json), else the one whose target lives in the source's own directory. A file compiled
only by a FOREIGN target borrows from its owner's surviving TUs. dinput/dinput8 and the
d3dx9_NN family share sources the same way. The two variants of one body are a cargo feature
(`wscript-rust/cscript`), not a second crate.

### A C macro that reads the CALLER's locals cannot be a plain `macro_rules!` port
**Symptom:** `no rules expected <ident>` at call sites that pass one argument more than the
macro takes, or E0425 for a local (`infoPtr`, `hwnd`) inside a prelude macro's expansion.
**Cause:** Wine's helper macros read locals they never take as parameters: comctl32's
`HIDDENBAND(a)` and `IsOnlySet(flags)` read `infoPtr`, `add_flag(a)` reads `dwFlags` and
`string`, and `REBAR_GetInfoPtr(wndPtr)` ignores its argument and reads `hwnd`. `macro_rules!`
hygiene hides a call site's locals from the macro body, so the faithful one-parameter port does
not resolve. Separately, the translated call sites guessed: most `HIDDENBAND` sites already
passed `infoPtr` first, a few did not. **Fix:** hand-port above the generated block (so a
replay keeps it), with each captured local as an explicit LEADING parameter, and make every call
site pass it. One parse error like this halts rustc before type checking, which also makes
crate-repair's pass look like it fixed everything (10 errors left, 0 applied).

### A UNICODE module inherits the ANSI TCHAR family from the `-sys` glob
`ntdll-sys` is generated WITHOUT `-DUNICODE`, so its bindgen carries `pub type LPTSTR = LPSTR;`.
A module built `set_module_type(<m> win32dll UNICODE)` picks that up through the island's
`pub use ntdll_sys::nt::*`, and every `LPTSTR`/`LPCTSTR`/`TCHAR` in the translation silently
means the NARROW type. aclui surfaced it loudly — `*mut i8` into `SetDlgItemTextW` — but that was
luck: the same alias inside `size_of::<TCHAR>()` compiles clean and sizes every buffer at half.
The A/W *function* aliases are usually derived into the crate prelude and the *type* family
forgotten; spell both, as explicit `pub use` re-exports that shadow the glob:
`LPWSTR as LPTSTR, LPCWSTR as LPCTSTR, PWSTR as PTSTR, PCWSTR as PCTSTR, WCHAR as TCHAR`.

The function side has a link-time twin: a worker that DECLARES the alias itself
(`extern "system" { fn DefMDIChildProc(..); }`, mmc_new) imports a name no DLL exports, an
undefined symbol on every arch. `port integrate` now gives such a declaration
`#[link_name = "DefMDIChildProcW"]` from the TU's own compile (`_aw_extern_link_names`, the
declaration side of `_aw_export_names`).

**And the prelude is not enough — the ISLAND has the same problem, one level lower.** The
re-exports above fix the module's own code; they do nothing for a struct the ISLAND declares.
desk.h says `TCHAR szPath[MAX_PATH]`, so with the glob's `TCHAR = c_char` bindgen emitted
`_ICON_PATH { szPath: [TCHAR; 260] }` — 260 bytes where the real struct is 520, on a module
compiled `-DUNICODE`. That compiles perfectly, and the translation had already papered over the
symptom by sprinkling `.cast()` on the call sites to make the narrow pointers fit. **Fix it in
the PROFILE, not the prelude**: `UNBLOCK="TCHAR PTCHAR TBYTE PTBYTE LPTSTR LPCTSTR PTSTR PCTSTR
LPTCH PTCH"` makes the module's own island emit them from its own `-DUNICODE` compile. The
check is one grep: `grep '^pub type TCHAR = ' src/types_i386.rs` must say `WCHAR`.
`scan_type_alias_contradictions` then reports the disagreement with ntdll-sys, which is real and
deliberate — baseline it, exactly as BCHAR already is for aclui/shell32/syssetup/winsrv.

**2026-10-08: mechanized, both halves.** The control panels re-hit it in 5 crates (27 stack
buffers at half size, `RegEnumValueW` told 128 WCHARs into 128 bytes), each needing a hand fix.
`profile_derive` now emits the TCHAR-family `UNBLOCK` for every UNICODE user-mode module, and
`port resolve` writes a generated `UNICODE TCHAR family` prelude block (`TCHAR = WCHAR` …)
whenever every TU's real compile command carries `-DUNICODE`. A `port fix` reply had already
built a shim casting `LPTSTR` to `*mut i8` around the wrong type -- delete such shims on sight.

**A TU that flips the charset is a template instantiation, not the module's charset.** fc's
texta.c opens `#undef UNICODE` / `#define _MBCS` and includes text.h; textw.c includes it
again wide. Merged into the module island, texta.c's toggles made the WHOLE island ANSI and
conutils.h `#error`ed. `profile_derive` now drops the toggles of a TU whose charset disagrees
with the module's (finding `CHARSET_INSTANTIATION`), and the Rust for the template is generic
over the char type, one instantiation exported per TU (fc-rust's `text_h.rs`).

### The same rule for TYPEDEFS: a private `type` alias that disagrees on WIDTH
The entry above is about shadow *structs*; this is the same disease one level down, and it is
cheaper to hit because a one-line `type X = ...;` does not look like a mirror at all.

**Symptom.** A green build on every arch, and a caller's stack local adjacent to an out-param
gets clobbered. No compiler, and no signature verifier, says anything.

**Cause.** Two files spell one C typedef differently and only the *resolved width* differs.
fastfat's `VBO` (`fat.h:38` = `ULONG32`, four bytes): the generated `types_<arch>.rs` islands
had it right, `dirsup.rs` said `type VBO = LARGE_INTEGER` and `dirctrl.rs` said `type VBO =
u64`. So `FatLocateDirent`, whose C prototype is `OUT PVBO ByteOffset`, stored
`(*ByteOffset).QuadPart` — an **eight-byte write through a pointer the interface says points
at four**. `create.rs`, `namesup.rs` and `fileinfo.rs` each backed that out-param with a `u32`
local, so every call lost 4 bytes of the caller's frame; `create.rs` is the file-OPEN path, and
arm64 boots FAT as its live system volume.

**Why it survived.** The two WRONG aliases agreed with each other — both 8 — so the definition
and its in-file callers were mutually consistent and only the honest callers were exposed.
`dirsup.rs` even carried a hand-rolled narrowing shim (`*ByteOffset = ByteOffsetLi.QuadPart as
u32`) at one site: someone met the mismatch, worked around it locally, and left the interface
wrong. **A local workaround for a width mismatch is a bug report against the type, not a fix.**

**Why no existing gate saw it.** Every single-arch build is green because each file is
internally consistent, and rustc has no reason to care what another file calls the same name.
`verify_c_signatures` compares the Rust decl against the C prototype — but both sides said
`PVBO` / `*mut VBO`, so the *names* agreed and only the resolutions differed. Only a whole-tree
read can catch this.

**Fix.** `tools/scan_type_alias_contradictions.py` now does that read, and the same-shaped
`scan_const_contradictions` is its sibling for values. Resolve against the C typedef, then
delete the private copies in favour of the generated island. Beyond VBO its first run found
`BOOLEAN = i32` in two fastfat files (DDK `BOOLEAN` is `unsigned char`) and `BOOL = u8` in
hidparser against `i32` in 22 others, the live one declaring `HidParser_UsesReportId -> BOOL`
for a function defined `-> u32` — benign only because the values are 0/1, so the low byte
happened to be the whole answer.

**The false positives are most of the work, and skipping them is what makes it trustworthy:**
